plan.summary: This 4-week block is the opening Building phase of a 12-week off-camp boxing plan. Week 1 establishes simple bodyweight performance baselines, then Weeks 2-4 build lower-body power, upper-body pushing and pulling strength, trunk stiffness, and a small amount of safe conditioning without adding unnecessary fatigue. With one session per week and bodyweight-only equipment, the plan keeps quality high, uses beginner-friendly exercises, and progresses mainly through cleaner reps, more control, and slightly harder variations.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength and explosive body control with simple low-impact power work and repeatable bodyweight basics.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Make the main bodyweight patterns harder and more explosive while keeping total fatigue easy to recover from around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Turn the earlier strength gains into sharper, faster outputs with crisp jumps, rapid upper-body intent, and low-fatigue conditioning.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can and land softly. Reset between reps so every jump stays crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want an even simpler jump variation. Start from a still quarter squat and jump hard.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: This is your baseline test for future progression. Use clean full-range reps, keep the body straight, and stop before form breaks.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log your best clean set so the app can track your bodyweight pressing progress.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, box, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if an incline is not available. Keep hips extended and range of motion full.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Control the descent, keep the front foot flat, and drive up smoothly. Use full range without rushing.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: A good swap if split squats bother your balance. Step back softly and keep your torso tall.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Row Under Sturdy Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Pull the chest toward the edge, pause briefly at the top, and keep the body rigid from shoulders to heels.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if you can anchor the towel safely. Keep reps smooth and stop if the setup feels unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Back Widows
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no safe row setup exists. Drive elbows into the floor and lift the chest slightly.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the lower back into the floor and keep ribs down. Shorten the lever if you cannot hold position cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is too hard. Move slowly and keep the lower back flat throughout.

exercises.name: Shadowboxing Tempo Intervals
exercises.notes: Stay relaxed and light on the feet. Keep technique sharp while the pace rises slightly each round.

endurancePrescription.rest: 1 minute easy walk and nasal breathing

substitutionOptions.name: Fast March Intervals
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight or you need a lower-skill conditioning option.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump hard on every rep and stick the landing quietly. Stop if height clearly drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler explosive option with less rhythm.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 clean reps in reserve on each set. Accelerate up hard without losing body position.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track reps completed at the target effort and aim to improve total quality reps over the block.

exercises.name: Split Squat
